messages:
customer_acme: Hey, our production app started getting 5-10s tail latency and a bunch of 401s around 09:12 UTC. Billing also jumped ~3x for that minute window. It looks like requests are routing to EU instead of us-west. Any idea?
anya_support: Ugh — sorry to hear that. Can you paste a couple request ids and the API key prefix? Did you change any failover/policy recently?
customer_acme: Req ids: req_8f3a, req_8f3b, req_8f3c. API key prefix: rk_live_abc123. We didn't touch infra; product said someone at Redwood saved a routing config around 09:10.
ops_bot: config-audit-bot: saved config 'failover_policy' by lucy_prod at 2026-11-07T09:10:23Z (cfg id cfg_993).
lucy_prod: I made a small change in the console to rebalance weights — intended to prefer us-west-2 (our primary). I didn't change tokens. I pushed the new ordering via the UI.
mike_sre: Looking at the router logs — many tokens that were previously hitting us-west-2 started getting routed to eu-central-1 at 09:10:24. The failover payload that hit the router is: 
```json
{"failover_policy":[{"region":"eu-central-1","priority":1,"weight":90,"sticky":true},{"region":"us-west-2","priority":0,"weight":10,"sticky":true}],"sticky_ttl_ms":30}
```
Router decision trace: selected region index 0 (eu-central-1) for most requests.
anya_support: That payload looks like the UI saved eu-central first despite the numeric priorities. Our parser currently uses array order as precedence (index 0 highest) — so array position > "priority" field. If the UI reorders the array but the user expects priority numbers to control precedence, that mismatch can flip where traffic goes.
customer_acme: That matches what we saw. But why 401s? Tokens should be global.
mike_sre: On Dedicated customers tokens are region-scoped for IAM — keys are bound to an account region. When a request lands in eu-central with a us-west token, auth failures (401) come back. The combination of wrong region + sticky behavior created quick auth churn and retries, amplifying latency and billing.
lucy_prod: Oh no — I changed the weight order in the UI and the console saved the array with EU first. I didn't realize the client code uses array order as truth. That's on me.
anya_support: For mitigation: 1) Temporary emergency override to pin this customer's key to us-west-2 at the routing layer. 2) Rollback the policy edit or reorder array so us-west-2 is first. 3) Increase sticky_ttl_ms so affinity persists across retries while we fix tokens. 4) We'll consider making the console warn about array-order vs priority numbers.
mike_sre: I can push an override now. Applying: `route_override: {api_key_prefix: "rk_live_abc123", region: "us-west-2", expires_at: +1h}` — done.
customer_acme: Confirming — latency back to normal for incoming checks. 401s gone for the last minute. Billing spike subsiding. Thank you.
lucy_prod: I submitted a rollback patch and a follow-up console change to ensure ordering is explicit (UI will show "primary/secondary" toggles instead of free reordering). PR: https://git.redwood.internal/p/r/4567
anya_support: We'll keep monitoring for 30m. Can you also confirm if you need us to reissue any region-bound keys?
customer_acme: No reissue needed now. We want root cause notes for our postmortem.
anya_support: Noted. I'll file a short incident summary and tag eng-runtime and product. Action items:
- rollback policy array ordering (lucy)
- console UX change to disambiguate order vs numeric priority (product)
- router to accept explicit `precedence` field rather than array order (eng-runtime)
- review default `sticky_ttl_ms` and surface small values in UI (eng-runtime/console)
Thanks all.
ops_bot: incident-tracker-bot: created incident INC-2026-1107-01 (routing-misorder) and assigned to eng-runtime,sla=high
mike_sre: Will follow up with logs slice + exact token failure counts in the incident ticket.
customer_acme: Appreciate the fast response.
